Exploring NVIDIA's risk and return

nvdastocks.Rmd
library(nvdastocks)

Who this is for

This guide is for anyone thinking about investing in NVIDIA who wants to know what that investment would have looked like in the past. The app answers the question: “If I had invested on a date I choose, how much would it be worth now, and how far would it have fallen along the way?””

Install and launch 

remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-dhoa0015-svg")

library(nvdastocks)
run_app()

The app opens in your browser, starts with a default of $1,000 investment made on 2 January 2020 to 2026.

Using the controls

All controls are on left sidebar:

  • Choose an investment period: the day you invest and the day you check its value. Any dates from 22 January 1999 to 21 September 2026 can be chosen.
  • Amount invested (US$): how much you put in at the start.
  • Compare growth in % (log scale): NVIDIA’s early prices were only cents, so on a normal chart the early years look flat. Tick this when looking at long periods to see how much those years really rose and fell.
  • Show 20- and 50-day averages (only shown in second tab only): adds lines that smooth out daily ups and downs, so the overall trend is easier to see.

Reading the two tabs

How much would I have gained?

The green line shows what your investment was worth on each day. The dashed orange line is the amount you put in, showing anything above it is a gain, and below it is a loss.

When did it fall, and how far?

The top chart is NVIDIA’s share price. The red chart underneath shows how far the price was below its highest point so far. At 0% the investment was at a new high; the deeper the red area, the bigger the fall.

Using the function directly

The app is built on investment_path(). It returns one row per trading day with the investment’s value value, the percentage gain gain_pct and the fall from its peak drawdown_pct.

path <- investment_path(nvda, "2020-01-01", "2026-09-21", amount = 1000)

# The last three trading days
tail(path[, c("date", "close", "value", "gain_pct", "drawdown_pct")], 3)
#>            date  close    value gain_pct drawdown_pct
#> 1686 2026-09-17 219.34 36819.69 3581.969    -6.744147
#> 1687 2026-09-18 222.27 37311.54 3631.154    -5.498408
#> 1688 2026-09-21 227.38 38169.34 3716.934    -3.325811

# The largest fall from a peak during the period (%)
min(path$drawdown_pct)
#> [1] -66.33509

Limitations

  • Prices are adjusted for NVIDIA’s share splits, so early prices look like cents. They are not the prices people paid at the time.
  • This is not the latest app since the data end on 21 September 2026. It could be made into one by using extensive feeding data tool.
  • The data come from a Kaggle dataset (CC BY-SA 4.0); see ?nvda for details.
